text: Given a site whose displayName exactly (case-insensitively) matches site_query, with a small (<=200,000 byte) UTF-8 text file named file_name in its document library root, When graph_read_site_file_text(site_query, file_name) is called once, Then the response contains the file's exact content plus site/drive/file metadata, and the caller never supplied a driveId or item id
Given no exact displayName match but exactly one keyword-search hit for site_query, When the tool is called, Then that single hit is used (no site_ambiguous) and the file is read successfully
Given a site_query matching no site at all, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = site_not_found with the search term echoed back, and makes no drive or file call

Given more than one keyword-search hit for site_query and none of them an exact displayName match, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = site_ambiguous with a candidate list (id, displayName, webUrl) matching the search results

Given a valid site_id is passed (with or without site_query), When the tool is called, Then site resolution uses site_id directly via GET /sites/{site_id} and the capturing client never receives a /sites?search= call
Given the file path 404s under a resolved drive, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = file_not_found with files_in_folder populated from the folder-listing call

Given the resolved path's item carries a folder facet instead of a file facet, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = file_not_found with a reason stating the path is a folder, not a file
Given the resolved site's /drive call 404s (no default document library), When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = file_not_found with a reason stating there is no document library
notes: source: dev — follows directly from the _resolve_drive branch, not independently required by the ticket's own AC list

text: Given the resolved file's size is 0 bytes, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = file_empty with the file's name and lastModifiedDateTime, and the capturing client's call list contains no /content call
Given the resolved file's size is 200,001 bytes, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = file_too_large with the actual size and the 200,000-byte limit, and no /content call is made
Given the resolved file's size is exactly 200,000 bytes (boundary), When the tool is called, Then it proceeds to fetch and return content (boundary uses > not >=)
Given the fetched content bytes fail UTF-8 decoding, When the tool is called, Then it returns error.code = not_text with the file's reported mimeType as file_type

Given two back-to-back calls using different simulated tokens/tenants (separate _CapturingClient instances) and different site/file names, When both calls run, Then neither call's site/drive/file resolution is reused by the other — the second call independently issues its own full resolution chain including its own site-search call
Given any successful or failing call to graph_read_site_file_text, When the call completes, Then every HTTP request recorded by the capturing client has method GET — never POST/PUT/DELETE
The ticket's own stated acceptance bar: 10 consecutive runs against a live tenant, zero malformed-id-style errors
steps: On a live, already-consented test tenant with a SharePoint site containing Permission Matrix.csv, run the real onboarding agent (or a scripted equivalent) calling graph_read_site_file_text(site_query="permission matrix", file_name="Permission Matrix.csv") 10 times back to back
Record the result of each of the 10 calls
expect: All 10 calls return the file's content successfully; zero calls fail with a malformed/invalid drive-id-style error
evidence: No live Entra/SharePoint tenant credentials available in this dev+test environment (gateway-mode service, sandbox has no Graph access token) -- cannot execute. Static evidence in lieu: src/graph_mcp/tools/sites.py's graph_read_site_file_text never emits a driveId/item id to the caller at any point in its success or error paths (verified by code review of the full function body, PRD-20413.md Tech design Data & API contract section); the structural guarantee this AC is actually about (one call, no id ever leaves the connector, see design doc's Open Questions) is covered by the green unit test test_read_site_file_text_happy_path_exact_site_match plus the full-chain TC1-TC14 unit suite (89 passed, 0 failed, uv run pytest). Needs: a consented test tenant with a SharePoint site + Permission Matrix.csv, run by whoever executes the dev+test leg with live credentials.

text: A real binary Office file triggers not_text with a sensible file_type reflecting Graph's actual MIME-type reporting (unit tests can only simulate the UTF-8 decode failure, not Graph's real mimeType value)
steps: On a live test tenant, place a real .xlsx or .docx file at a known site/path
expect: error.code = not_text, with file_type reflecting the real MIME type Graph reports for that file (e.g. application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
evidence: No live Entra/SharePoint tenant credentials available in this dev+test environment -- cannot execute against a real binary file. Static/simulated evidence in lieu: test_read_site_file_text_binary_content_returns_not_text (tests/test_tools.py) drives the exact same code path (src/graph_mcp/tools/sites.py graph_read_site_file_text's UnicodeDecodeError branch) with a simulated non-UTF-8 byte string and a simulated file facet mimeType, asserting error.code == 'not_text' and file_type echoed from the resolved item's file.mimeType -- green (uv run pytest, 89 passed). What this cannot prove locally: that Graph's real root:/{path}: response actually populates the file.mimeType facet with a sensible value for a real .xlsx/.docx at that tenant -- that part is specifically what TC16 exists to check live. Needs: a consented test tenant with a real binary Office file at a known site/path, run by whoever executes the dev+test leg with live credentials.
